limitations: 18 cases contain 35 unresolved reference fields. Their null labels are retained; unresolved references preclude PASS under B17_POLICY.
The Slovak-language quality of generated notes cannot be reviewed before inference; it requires independent post-run linguistic assessment, not a heuristic.
B17 inputs are distinct from exact normalized B14 inputs, but some reuse the same broad intent scenarios by design.
No network access, model inference, or production operation was performed.
rationale: Reviewed all 100 synthetic SK/CS/EN/HU cases and all 800 reference fields against the B1.7 brief, existing email-monitoring system prompt and eight-field contract, and inherited B1.6 distinctions. Explicit unconditional agreement is labeled as consent; conditional or context-dependent intent remains false only when the message clearly withholds present consent, and null where intent is genuinely ambiguous. Explicit current-service cancellation is labeled true with critical alert; information requests, quotations, and explicit negations are not cancellations, while indirect or contradictory intent remains null. Rejection of a new offer is distinguished from cancellation of an existing service and follows the inherited negative sentiment/warning convention. Objective complaints retain the inherited critical alert. Anger, rude/disrespectful language, and profanity are treated as distinct dimensions; quoted phrases are not attributed as the sender's intent. SYN-B17-092 now correctly has wantsConsent=true: it explicitly assents to the second item, while saying that assent is not to the contract; the system prompt defines consent broadly as agreeing to something. Ambiguity remains explicit, and the approval authorizes only isolated inference, not a PASS conclusion or production use.
